reason: The platform cron runner (systemScope) scans due schedules across all workspaces and claims each one by the schedule id read in that same scan; it serves no tenant request.
listIncidents() with no workspace is the platform-wide security incident feed; the only route passes the caller's workspace, which uses scoped().
SSO sign-in resolves a connection by its id or by the user's email domain before any workspace is known; the matched row is what names the workspace.
A one-time SSO auth request is looked up and consumed by its unguessable state value on the identity-provider callback, before any workspace is known.
An incoming API key is authenticated by its hash before any workspace is known; the matched row is what establishes the workspace.
Queue workers dequeue and claim jobs across all workspaces by queue name or job id; they serve no tenant request.
An inbound webhook resolves its subscription by the public subscription id in its URL, before any workspace is known; the row establishes the workspace.
An inbound webhook resolves its endpoint by the public slug in its URL, before any workspace is known; the row establishes the workspace.
Inbound webhook verification unseals the signing secret named by the subscription's connection_ref, a platform-wide primary key. Follow-up: also bind the subscription's workspace_id.
